learning_outcomes.text: Explain what a distributed ledger is and how it differs from a traditional database
Describe how blocks, hashes and chaining make a ledger tamper-evident
Distinguish public, private and permissioned networks and their trust assumptions
Trace how a transaction moves from submission to finality on a public chain
Evaluate when a blockchain is and is not the right tool for a problem
Explain the economic and governance forces that keep a decentralised network running

integrative_case: A regional produce cooperative wants a shared record of shipments across 12 independent farms and 3 distributors; decide whether a blockchain fits, choose a network type, and justify the trust and governance trade-offs to the board.
